questions.q: A man weighs 80 kg. He stands on a weighing scale in a lift which is moving upwards with a uniform acceleration of 6 m/s$^2$. What would be his weight in kg? (g = 10 m/s$^2$)
questions.explanation: Apparent weight (in kg) = $m\dfrac{g+a}{g}=80\times\dfrac{16}{10}=128$ kg.

questions.q: A mass M is hung with a light inextensible string as shown in figure. Find the tension of the horizontal string. [Figure: a mass M hangs vertically from point O; O is connected to a wall by a horizontal string and to the ceiling by a string inclined at 45° to the ceiling]
questions.explanation: At O, resolving forces: the inclined string's vertical component balances Mg, $T\sin45^\circ=Mg$, and its horizontal component equals the horizontal string's tension, $T\cos45^\circ=T_h$. Since $\sin45^\circ=\cos45^\circ$, $T_h=Mg$.

questions.q: A wooden block of mass M lies on a rough floor. Another wooden block of the same mass is hanging from the point O through strings as shown in the figure. To achieve equilibrium, the co-efficient of static friction between the block on the floor with the floor itself is [figure: block M on floor connected by a horizontal string to point O; from O another string goes up at angle θ to a wall/ceiling, and a third string hangs straight down from O holding a second block M]
questions.explanation: At O: $T\sin\theta = Mg$ (supports hanging block) and $T\cos\theta$ equals the friction force $\mu Mg$ on the floor block. Dividing, $\tan\theta = 1/\mu$, so $\mu=\cot\theta$.

questions.q: A block of certain mass is placed on a rough floor. The coefficients of static and kinetic friction between the block and the floor are 0.4 and 0.25 respectively. A constant horizontal force F = 20 N acts on it so that the velocity of the block varies with time according to the following graph. The mass of the block is nearly (Take g ≃ 10 ms$^{-2}$) [graph: v (m/s) on y-axis reaching 20 at t = 3 s, straight line through origin]
questions.explanation: From the graph $a=20/3\approx6.7\,ms^{-2}$. Using $F-\mu_k mg=ma$: $20-2.5m=6.7m$, giving $m\approx2.2$ kg.

questions.q: A block of certain mass is placed on a rough inclined plane. The angle between the plane and the horizontal is $30^0$. The coefficients of static and kinetic frictions between the block and the inclined plane are 0.6 and 0.5 respectively. Then the magnitude of the acceleration of the block is [Take g=10 ms$^{-2}$]
questions.explanation: Maximum static friction $=\mu_smg\cos30^\circ\approx0.52mg$ exceeds the driving force $mg\sin30^\circ=0.5mg$, so the block remains at rest and the acceleration is zero.

questions.q: A body of mass 10 kg is kept on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the body and the surface is 0.5. A horizontal force of 60 N is applied on the body. The resulting acceleration of the body is about
questions.explanation: Friction force = μmg = 0.5×10×10 = 50 N. Net force = 60 − 50 = 10 N, so a = 10/10 = 1 ms$^{-2}$.

questions.q: Two masses of 5 kg and 3 kg are suspended with the help of massless inextensible strings as shown in the figure [ceiling → T$_1$ → 5 kg → T$_2$ → 3 kg, the whole system moving upward with acceleration 2 m s$^{-2}$]. When the whole system is going upwards with acceleration 2 m/s$^2$, the value of T$_1$ is (use g = 9.8 m/s$^2$)
questions.explanation: T$_1$ supports both masses accelerating upward: $T_1=(m_1+m_2)(g+a)=(5+3)(9.8+2)=8\times11.8=94.4$ N.

questions.q: A car is moving in a circular horizontal track of radius 10 m with a constant speed of 10 m s$^{-1}$. A bob is suspended from the roof of the car by a light wire of length 1.0 m. The angle made by the wire with the vertical is (in radian)
questions.explanation: $\tan\theta=\dfrac{v^2}{rg}=\dfrac{100}{10\times9.8}\approx1$, so $\theta\approx\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

questions.q: A coin placed on a rotating turn table just slips if it is placed at a distance of 4 cm from the centre. If the angular velocity of the turn table is doubled it will just slip at a distance of:
questions.explanation: Slipping condition: $\mu m g = m\omega^2 r \Rightarrow r\propto \dfrac{1}{\omega^2}$. Doubling $\omega$ reduces $r$ to $\dfrac{4}{4}=1$ cm.

questions.q: One end of a string of length 'l' is connected to a particle of mass 'm' and the other to a small peg on a smooth horizontal table. If the particle moves in a circle with speed 'v', the net force on the particle (directed towards the centre) is: (T is the tension in the string)
questions.explanation: The string tension alone supplies the required centripetal force, so the net force towards the centre is just T (which equals $mv^2/l$).

questions.q: An object with mass 5 kg is acted upon by a force, $\vec F = (-3\hat i + 4\hat j)$ N. If its initial velocity at t = 0 is $\vec v = (6\hat i - 12\hat j)$ ms$^{-1}$, the time at which it will just have a velocity along y-axis is
questions.explanation: Acceleration $\vec a = \vec F/m = (-0.6\hat i + 0.8\hat j)$ ms$^{-2}$; velocity is along the y-axis when the x-component vanishes: $6 - 0.6t = 0 \Rightarrow t = 10$ s.

questions.q: A block rests on a rough inclined plane making an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the plane is 0.8. If the frictional force on the block is 10 N, the mass of the block is (g = 10 ms$^{-2}$)
questions.explanation: Since the block is at rest (equilibrium), friction balances the component of weight along the incline: f = mg sin30°. So 10 = m(10)(0.5) ⟹ m = 2 kg.

questions.q: A man weighing 60 kg is in a lift moving down with an acceleration of 1.8 ms$^{-2}$. The force exerted by the floor on him is
A body of mass 50 kg. is suspended using a spring balance inside a lift at rest. If the lift starts falling freely, the reading of the spring balance is
questions.explanation: In free fall the lift and body are both in a state of weightlessness (apparent weight = 0), so the spring balance reads zero.

questions.q: Maximum acceleration of the train in which a 50 kg box lying on its floor will remain stationary (Given: Co-efficient of static friction between the box and the train's floor is 0.3 and g = 10 ms$^{-2}$)
questions.explanation: The box stays stationary relative to the train as long as required force $ma \le \mu mg$, so $a_{max} = \mu g = 0.3 \times 10 = 3.0$ ms$^{-2}$.

questions.q: A stone of mass 0.05 kg is thrown vertically upwards. What is the direction and magnitude of net force on the stone during its upward motion?
questions.explanation: Neglecting air resistance, the only force acting is gravity: F = mg = 0.05 × 9.8 = 0.49 N, directed vertically downwards throughout the motion.

questions.q: A person is driving a vehicle at uniform speed of 5 ms$^{-1}$ on a level curved track of radius 5 m. The coefficient of static friction between tyres and road is 0.1. Will the person slip while taking the turn with the same speed? Take g = 10 ms$^{-2}$. Choose the correct statement.
options: A person will slip if v$^2$ > 5 ms$^{-1}$
A person will not slip if v$^2$ > 10 ms$^{-1}$
A person will slip if v$^2$ = 5 ms$^{-1}$
A person will slip if v$^2$ < 5 ms$^{-1}$
questions.explanation: Maximum safe speed satisfies v$^2$ = $\mu$gr = 0.1\times10\times5 = 5; the person slips if v$^2$ exceeds this value (here v$^2$=25>5, so slips).

questions.q: An aeroplane executes a horizontal loop at a speed of 720 kmph with its wings banked at 45$^{\circ}$. What is the radius of the loop? Take g = 10 ms$^{-2}$.
In a lift moving up with an acceleration of 5 ms$^{-2}$, a ball is dropped from a height of 1.25 m. The time taken by the ball to reach the floor of the lift is ...... (nearly) (g = 10 ms$^{-2}$)
questions.explanation: Inside the accelerating lift, the effective gravity is $g'=g+a=15\ \text{ms}^{-2}$. Using $h=\dfrac{1}{2}g't^2$, $t=\sqrt{2h/g'}=\sqrt{2(1.25)/15}\approx0.41\text{ s}\approx0.4\text{ s}$.

questions.q: A gun fires a small bullet with kinetic energy K. Then kinetic energy of the gun while recoiling is
questions.explanation: By momentum conservation the gun and bullet have equal and opposite momentum $p$. Since $KE=p^2/2m$, the much heavier gun (larger $m$) has a smaller kinetic energy than the bullet's $K$.

questions.q: A block kept on a rough surface starts sliding when the inclination of the surface is '$\theta$' with respect to the horizontal. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the surface is
questions.explanation: Sliding begins when mg sin$\theta$ = $\mu_s$ mg cos$\theta$, i.e. $\mu_s=\tan\theta$.

questions.q: Block $A$ of mass 2 kg is placed over block $B$ of mass 8 kg. The combination is placed over a rough horizontal surface. Coefficient of friction between $B$ and the floor is 0.5. Coefficient of friction between $A$ and $B$ is 0.4. A horizontal force of 10 N is applied on block $B$. The force of friction between $A$ and $B$ is ..................... ($g = 10\, ms^{-2}$).
questions.explanation: Maximum friction from the floor on the combined 10 kg is $0.5\times10\times10 = 50$ N, greater than the applied 10 N, so the whole system stays at rest; since no force is applied directly on $A$, it needs no friction force to stay in equilibrium, so the friction between $A$ and $B$ is zero.

questions.q: A ball rests upon a flat piece of paper on a table top. The paper is pulled horizontally but quickly towards right [the ball sits on the paper, an arrow shows the paper being pulled right]. Relative to its initial position with respect to the table, the ball ............ a) remains stationary if there is no friction between the paper and the ball. b) moves to the left and starts rolling backwards, i.e. to the left if there is a friction between the paper and the ball. c) moves forward, i.e. in the direction in which the paper is pulled. Here, the correct statement/s is/are .................
questions.explanation: By inertia, without friction the ball stays at rest relative to the table (a); with friction, the sudden jerk gives the paper's surface a brief backward-relative impulse on the ball, making it roll back to the left relative to the table (b) (as per KEA key).

questions.q: A body of mass 0.05 kg is observed to fall with an acceleration of $9.5\ \text{ms}^{-2}$. The opposing force of air on the body is ______ ($g = 9.8\ \text{ms}^{-2}$).
questions.explanation: Net force $= m(g-a) = 0.05\times(9.8-9.5) = 0.05\times0.3 = 0.015\ \text{N}$, which is the air resistance opposing the fall.

questions.q: Three concurrent co-planar forces 1 N, 2 N and 3 N acting along different directions on a body
options: can keep the body in equilibrium if 1 N and 2 N act at right angles.
cannot keep the body in equilibrium.
can keep the body in equilibrium if 1 N and 3 N act at an acute angle.
can keep the body in equilibrium if 2 N and 3 N act at right angles.
questions.explanation: The maximum possible resultant of the 1 N and 2 N forces is 3 N, and only when they are collinear (0° apart) — at any other angle (right angle, acute angle, etc.) their resultant is less than 3 N and can never balance the 3 N force, so equilibrium is impossible.
